featured_reviews.review_text: Had gone here for a takeaway order of prawns sukka Mangalorean style. The taste was absolutely home made. It was 6-Apr-2024 when UPI and bank servers were down. featured_reviews.name: prathamesh satle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am giving a one-star rating solely for the owner's dedication because they personally cook the food in their own kitchen. However, I wouldn't recommend it to others. The service was not satisfactory; there were no spoons for eating, and glasses were not provided for drinking water. Even the food itself wasn't served properly; it felt like we were left to fend for ourselves. The main issue was the long wait time, almost 45 minutes, just to get the main course. Because of this, it seemed like the food was hastily prepared, which is why I feel compelled to leave this review.

Online delivery orders seem to be given higher priority, while there's considerable delay for dining-in customers.

This was my first and last visit to that hotel.

So please take this feedback into consideration.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been visiting this place for my weekend dinners as I’am a hardcore seafood lover and a taste coming from Koli style food truck was heaven .

I have tried almost everything from Surmai kalvan to their pan fried fishes to chicken thali and mutton too .

The taste is very much homely and they make everything from scratch with freshness . Nothing is stale or bitter.

Another thing is that they strongly BELIVE in “Atithi Devi Bhava” which states guest is god . Everytime to go to this place Riva and Manoj kaka especially has treated me like a home member and not just a customer .

They have grown a lot because of their relationship building with customer and the great taste that they deliver in Thakur village .

In a week usually it’s twice or thrice that I pay visit to this place and it’s hands down .

I personally recommend this to all the seafood Koli style food lovers who are searching for pocket friendly and delicious maharashtrian meals .

Guys, it’s authentic .

Keep up the good work .

5 stars to everything

featured_reviews.name: Bhukkad Girl
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to experience the real thrill of eating seafood in a clay pot in Kandivali, there's no better place than this.
.

Here you can try authentic seafood platters,
and the seafood is so amazing
that you just want to keep eating.

This is Tarri Restaurant.

Started by a Marathi couple, this place
has a women-led kitchen
and the ambience is perfect for full family dine-ins and celebrations.

I tried here —
bombil fry,
surmai fry,
paplet thali,
chicken vade thali,
squid fry
and shrimp rice.

The fish is so fresh
and the taste is so addictive
that once you eat it
it is hard to stop.

And this chicken kharda is
so tasty
that you will really fall in love with it.

So if you are a seafood lover and want to have a relaxing meal with your family, then definitely try this once.

featured_reviews.name: Clara Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
Amazing Food, Chicken Kharda was awesome.  We had ordered for veg as well as non veg starters each were very tasty and fresh.

Chicken handi, Mutton handi, Prawns cutlet, Bombil fry, Prawns pulao all too good.

Fish served was fresh and very tasty.

Ac room was enough to hold a family get together for 20 people

And lastly the Sol kadhi was the cherry in cake.

The staff was very supportive and service was very very good.

Recommend strongly for all the nonveg eaters quenching for authentic style Malwani Food.

featured_reviews.name: THE SIMPLE SOUL
featured_reviews.review_text:
Umm..nice Thali experience. We didn't have to wait for a table coz we got there early.
Space is very cramped though. Only 4 tables in the AC section, that too, 2 of them sharing a boundary with the washroom...ewww..not good for a dine out.
The thali is very basic. Rice, curry, bhakri/chapatis, sliced onion, whatever fried fish you order & dried prawns. 🍤🐟That's it. No solkadi, no desert, no salad. Nothing.
For the price, not VFM.

Only 1 boy to take orders from all tables + handle the Zomato/ Swiggy orders. He was rushed.
Yet, he was polite and courteous. Good going.

The gravy is extremely spicy 🔥🥵. Not for the faint-hearted. Had to forego half of it.
The fish is fresh, though.

Several patrons who asked for BOMBIL, were turned down bcz it wasn't available. Not great, since a seafood place ought to have these by default (one of the crowd favourites). Or ..perhaps ...being a Sunday, Tarri was trying to push the other costlier fish..who knows?? 🤔Anyways, the portion of fried prawns was decent.
No soft drinks available besides the bottled fizzies. The soft drinks were all warm & not chilled or cool post 12 noon. 🥤
And solkadi, which was just made, was not cooled before serving, post 1 p.m.
No desserts, except kharvas (decent) & caramel custard.🍮
Return if you want to sample other dishes, if not, would not recommend a second visit.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sarova Restaurant and Bar has always caught my eye while passing by the highway—there’s something inviting about its look and location. When I finally stopped by, I was genuinely impressed with the interior and rooftop section. It has a cozy, laid-back vibe that’s rare to find in a highway-side bar. The ambiance feels just right for a casual drink or quick hangout, especially in the evenings.

But unfortunately, that’s where the positives ended for me.

The food and service were a big letdown. I ordered chicken lollipop, but the head waiter kept insisting I try the tandoor version instead. When I clearly told him I wasn’t interested and that I’d rather skip it if the regular lollipop wasn’t available, he suddenly said, “We do have the lollipop.” It felt very manipulative and pushy.

A similar thing happened with the veg starters. We ordered mushroom, but they brought paneer instead—and again, the waiter tried hard to convince us to just go with it. When we refused, he said mushroom would take 20 minutes. We agreed to wait, but then suddenly he claimed they were out of mushrooms altogether. This kind of flip-flop and forceful attitude really ruined the experience.

Food quality was average at best, and the overall attitude of the staff made it feel like they were more interested in pushing what’s convenient for them than giving the customer what they want.

In summary: Beautiful setting, poor service. Will I return? Only if it’s just for a drink—not for food.

featured_reviews.name: kavita bekal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually write reviews when I truly like a place, but I felt the need to share this experience because my stomach was upset after eating here, which is concerning.

I visited this restaurant expecting authentic Ratnagiri/Konkan food, especially given the name and the 4-star rating. Unfortunately, the food did not meet those expectations at all.

I ordered a fish thali, but there was nothing about it that reflected true Konkan or Ratnagiri cuisine. The fish fry was bland, not properly marinated, and lacked basic flavor. I had to add salt, pepper, and lime myself just to make it edible. Authentic Konkan fish fry is known for its seasoning and marinade, which was completely missing here.

The fish curry was a simple onion-based gravy with no depth—no kokum, no tamarind, no spice, and not even the correct color of a traditional fish curry. The thali included bhakri, rice, fish fry, fish curry, sol curry, and a dry fish preparation. Except for the dry item, nothing tasted authentic or satisfying.

I also ordered chicken sukka, which is supposed to be dry and at least mildly spicy. What was served was more like a regular chicken curry with gravy, not dry at all, and completely lacking spice and flavor. It did not resemble chicken sukka in any way.

I had high expectations, but the food was nowhere near what one would expect from a place claiming to serve Ratnagiri or Konkan cuisine. This food does not represent Konkan food, not even remotely.

Overall, a very disappointing experience, and due to both the quality of the food and the health issue afterward, I would not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Prasad Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hospitality destroyed by arrogance, not service.

We visited this restaurant with a family group of ten, including two elderly parents, in-laws, women, and one little child. Despite a confirmed booking, the manager reserved sofa seating for fourteen people who never arrived. When I politely asked about this, he dismissed me saying “Aapko nahi samaj ayega.” Later, when I called him over for ordering A bhai idhar aa, he publicly warned me in front of my whole family: “Aap kerke bulao.”

Such language is not only disrespectful but can traumatize children and elders. I was not under the influence of alcohol—had anyone been drinking, this could easily have escalated into a brawl. As a regular customer, I now wonder how I can return, especially if the same staff continues to treat guests this way. In Bombay, saying “Tu” is common language, but in this restaurant a professional setting staff should be addressed respectfully as Aap—especially when they are around 38 years of age.

Maybe the guy manager was bothered by my cross-question about the booking. But if he had simply explained that the sofa was booked prior to mine, or assured me that we would be shifted if no one showed up, I would have been satisfied. If tone or disrespect was a concern, he could have asked the owner not to assign him the task of dealing with me. There were many professional ways to handle the situation, but instead he chose to insult me in front of my family.

Hospitality should be about dignity and respect. Management must take this seriously and train staff so no other family faces such humiliation in the future is my humble request to the owner of the beautiful and one of the best restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: SAMEER SAHU
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ebony Fine Dine absolutely deserves every single one of these 5 stars. The experience was luxury and comfort at the exact same time — extremely hard balance to pull off and they nailed it.
Service was phenomenal — attentive without hovering. Staff knew the menu, had actual real recommendations (not generic upsell scripts) and the pacing of courses was honestly perfect.
The food was outstanding. Every single dish was seasoned beautifully, plated like art and tasted even better than it looked. You can tell there is actual technique + real love in the kitchen. Portions and value also surprised me you leave satisfied and not overwhelmed.
Ambience was romantic, premium, modern, and they kept sound levels where you can actually speak normally without yelling which I appreciate so much.
If you’re looking for a place that feels special, memorable, and truly elevated go to Ebony Fine Dine. This is a restaurant that understands both hospitality and culinary craft at a high level. I will 100% be coming back and telling everyone about this place.

featured_reviews.name: Krish Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Propaganda I keep falling for is amazing food and even better desserts. Ebony Casual Dinner is the ultimate vibe, serving mouthwatering food in generous portions. We started with two drinks: Peppery Crush and Blue Breeze, both unique and refreshing. The Peppery Crush really stood out. For starters, the Cottage Cheese Balls with Sparkling Spinach were a hit, paired perfectly with peanut sauce - spicy, sweet, and tangy all at once. Next, the Mushroom Maska Chaska, served in a matka, was as expected, delicious. The mushroom was juicy and charred to perfection, with a flawless sauce. However, the Hot Pot Noodles were skippable. We ended on a high note with the Espresso Whiskey Caramel Brownie Sundae, one of the best desserts. The caramel's sweetness paired impeccably with the whiskey's bitterness. This place has it all; definitely worth a visit. Follow @burpsandslurps on Instagram for more food adventures.
